answer: Witnessed resource custody: each identity must hold a distinct physical site with a metered power feed and water draw, attested by independent sensors. A single operator cannot occupy two separated sites along the river without duplicate utility records and transport logs. So the registry binds identity to a geotagged meter that a garden's irrigation pump or a ridge's relay station keeps reporting. Duplicating one costs real land, wiring, and months of readings, capping how many identities any one operator can afford.
